summary:
Session 2026-11-11.

Session 2026-11-11 pre-open. Held META, MSFT and PLTR, with cash about 71%. No orders.

Yesterday SPY fell 0.37%, QQQ fell 0.68% and XLK fell 1.15%. NVDA closed down 5.5%.

Premarket today is a broad AI-infrastructure rebound after CoreWeave earnings (a $133B backlog, stock up about 15%, with Chanos criticising its returns on capital):
- NVDA +3.9%
- AMD +5.8%
- AVGO +4.3%
- META +1.5%
- TSLA +1.7%
- GOOGL +1.2%
- PLTR +2.4%
- AMZN +0.6%
- MSFT +0.4%
- AAPL -0.4%

I did not chase the gap-ups, because the move rests on a single peer's earnings headline and the day-to-day swings are large. I did not re-enter NVDA, because the investigation headline is still unresolved. I did not find the October CPI print or its market reaction (it was due 11-10).

Candidates examined and not traded: GOOGL, AMZN, AMD, AVGO, NVDA.

Next session:
- Check the CPI and Fed-hike narrative.
- Look at GOOGL and AMZN on any dip.
- Revisit NVDA once there is news on the investigation.
- Stops: META 571.8, MSFT 483.6, PLTR 143.
- Horizons end 11-24 (PLTR) and 11-27 (META and MSFT).
notes:
Session 1 (2026-10-29): Started 100% cash. Bought MSFT, NVDA, META, AVGO, AAPL, PLTR. Skipped AMZN/GOOGL/TSLA/AMD.
Session 2 (10-30): AMZN missed Q3, capex funding worry overrode capex plans. Held all.
Session 3 (11-02): Oct 30 QQQ -3.5%, SOX -7%. Held everything.
Session 11-06/09: NVDA stopped out -9.6% (gap through stop at open on CEO Huang affair / Megaspeed spy investigation headline). Lesson: stops don't protect against overnight gaps; key-man headline risk gaps. Position sizing small (6.8%) limited damage.
Session 11-10: Mon 11-09 big rebound (SPY +2.4%, QQQ +3.5%, AMD +13%, AVGO +8.8%, META +5%). CPI released 8:30 ET today (consensus +0.3% headline, core +0.2%); Dec Fed hike ~80% priced. Held META/MSFT/PLTR, cash ~71%. Did not chase after a +2-13% day before CPI.
Tools: web_search sometimes returns JSON string (json.loads); pre-open IEX in get_quotes shows gaps.
Next: check CPI reaction, deploy cash on dips (GOOGL/AMZN candidates), re-evaluate NVDA re-entry once the investigation is clarified. Stops: META 571.8, MSFT 483.6, PLTR 143.
prompt:
Your universe is exactly ten stocks: NVDA, AAPL, MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN, META, TSLA, AVGO, AMD and PLTR,
plus cash. Nothing else is allowed.

- Your job is to decide how much of each of the ten to hold long or short, and when to hold cash
  instead, based on news and evidence about these companies, their suppliers, customers and
  competitors, and the macro events that move them.
- One of the benchmarks is these same ten stocks held at equal weight and never traded, so every
  trade you make has to beat doing nothing with the same names. Trading costs 0.10% per side.
- These are the most analysed stocks in the world. An edge, if there is one, comes from reading
  fresh information carefully and acting only when it changes the picture.
